propositions.text: Claimant is a Colombian citizen seeking refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(a) and (b).
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXXX XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Colombia claims refugee protection pursuant to Sections 96 and 97(1)(a) and (b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).1

paragraphs.summary: The claimant, a Colombian citizen, seeks refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(a) and (b).

propositions.text: The claimant alleges facts supporting his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged the following in support of his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges facts supporting his refugee claim.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges FARC seeks him due to perceived political opinion after a 2009 incident involving denied medical assistance.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that due to an incident in XXXX, Department of Tolima, Colombia at the end of XXXX 2009, when an injured member of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), with others in his band, arrived at the house of his brother, where the claimant was, demanding medical assistance and did not get it, that he is sought by the FARC, because he is perceived as having a political opinion contrary to the FARC.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges FARC seeks him for perceived opposing political opinion after a 2009 incident denying medical help.

propositions.text: During the incident, FARC demanded brother-in-law get a doctor and kept claimant and sister as guarantees; shots were heard then quiet.
propositions.quote: In this incident, the Guerilla demanded that the claimant's brother-in-law go to town to get a doctor, and that the claimant and sister remain at the house as guarantees. While the brother-in-law was gone, the claimant was in the kitchen, when more shots were heard, then quiet; the injured party left with the others who had accompanied him.

paragraphs.summary: During the incident, FARC demanded brother-in-law get a doctor and kept claimant and sister as guarantees; shots were heard then quiet.

propositions.text: Brother-in-law returned alone as no one else was willing to come.
propositions.quote: The brother-in-law returned, alone, as no one was willing to come.

paragraphs.summary: Brother-in-law returned alone as no one else was willing to come.

propositions.text: Claimant and family fled the house separately fearing FARC's return.
propositions.quote: Fearing the FARC's return, the claimant and his family quickly left the house, and went their separate ways.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant and family fled the house separately fearing FARC's return.

propositions.text: While hiding in Bogota, claimant learned FARC inquired about him and sister, claiming they made FARC victims.
propositions.quote: Later while hiding in Bogota, the claimant learned that the FARC went to his sister's to inquire about him and his sister in-law, because the FARC claimed that the claimant and his family had made them "victims" in XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: While hiding in Bogota, claimant learned FARC inquired about him and sister, claiming they made FARC victims.

propositions.text: Claimant believes he is perceived as politically opposed to FARC for denying medical assistance.
propositions.quote: As a result the claimant believes that he is perceived as having a political opinion which is contrary to the interests of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) because he did not provide the medical assistance to the FARC that day.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant believes he is perceived as politically opposed to FARC for denying medical assistance.

propositions.text: Claimant is not a Convention refugee due to lack of well-founded fear of persecution for a Convention ground in Colombia.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant is not a Convention refugee as he does not have a well-founded fear of persecution for a Convention ground in Colombia.

propositions.text: Claimant is not in need of protection; removal to Colombia poses no personal risk to life or cruel treatment.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant is not a person in need of protection in that his removal to Colombia would not subject him personally to a risk to his life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, or to a danger of torture.

propositions.text: Determinative issues are credibility, subjective fear, and re-availment of the claimant.
propositions.quote: The determinative issue is credibility, subjective fear, and re-availment of the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds claimant is not a Convention refugee or in need of protection; key issues are credibility, subjective fear, and re-availment.

propositions.text: Assessment considered claimant's oral and written testimony, counsel's oral submissions, and all documentary evidence at hearing.
propositions.quote: In making the assessment in this claim the panel considered the claimant's oral and written testimony, counsel's submissions made orally, and all other documentary evidence entered at the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The panel considered claimant's testimony, counsel's submissions, and documentary evidence in assessment.

propositions.text: Claimant's Colombian citizenship accepted based on identification at Port of Entry including passport and US Permanent Residence Card.
propositions.quote: I accept that the claimant is a citizen of Colombia due to the identification provided at the Port of Entry,2 which included his Colombian Passport and United States Permanent Residence Card.

paragraphs.summary: The court accepts claimant's Colombian citizenship based on identification documents.

propositions.text: Maldonado requires acceptance of testimony as truthful unless good reason to doubt veracity.
propositions.quote: Maldonado3 requires the panel to accept as truthful, testimony, unless there is good reason to doubt the veracity.

paragraphs.summary: Maldonado requires accepting testimony as truthful unless there is good reason to doubt it.

propositions.text: There were inconsistencies in claimant's story, such as who he lived with.
propositions.quote: There were inconsistencies in the claimant's story such as: * Who he lived with.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds inconsistencies in claimant's story about who he lived with.

propositions.text: Claimant stated he lived in a small village with wife in Tolima from 2005, living peacefully.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated in the narrative that he had lived in a small village "I went to live with my wife in the town of XXXX, Department of Tolima, where my brother has a small house he gave me to use in exchange for taking care of it. In the following years we found a degree of peace..."4 According to the narrative, he lived peacefully with his wife.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant stated he lived peacefully with his wife in a small village in Tolima from 2005.

propositions.text: Letters provided do not corroborate claimant's residence or family members; documents inconsistent and vague.
propositions.quote: The claimant provided a letter5 certifying that the "XXXX XXXX family resided at the property". This letter does not say who the members of the family were, and if the claimant was one of them. As a result it is not useful to corroborate whom the claimant lived with and whether, he himself lived there. The claimant provided a second letter6 that stated that by 2004, the "XXXX family" was living in the particular house, "by the year 2004" however this date may refer to the claimant's sister and brother-in-law, or even brother who owned the house, but it does not corroborate that the claimant lived there, because the date mentioned is inconsistent with the date that the claimant alleged to have started living there, which was in 2005.7 Considering the two documents, the claimant's narrative and testimony, they are inconsistent and vague in what they are supposed to be confirming; the panel does not find them useful. This inconsistency, and vagueness, together with the claimant's testimony and narrative, raises a negative inference in the panel's mind as to the claimant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds letters and claimant's narrative inconsistent and vague, raising negative credibility inference.

propositions.text: Claimant's testimony about who was present during FARC event was inconsistent; wife was not there.
propositions.quote: When asked about the evening of the event with the FARC, "who was with you?" He answered "Sister, husband, and neighbor from the house next door." The panel further asked him, "Was your wife there?" he replied "No".

paragraphs.summary: Claimant testified wife was not present during FARC event, inconsistent with other statements.

propositions.text: Claimant's oral testimony about living arrangements inconsistent with narrative; wife visited only briefly and infrequently.
propositions.quote: The claimant had said in the hearing room that he was living in the village for approximately 4 years, from 2005-2009, however the wife, only came for short periods, at limited periods, 3 to 4 times a year. He stated that sometimes he lived with himself and his wife, and sometimes with his brother and sister XXXX. The panel found the claimant's oral testimony inconsistent with the narrative.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's oral testimony about living arrangements is inconsistent with narrative; wife visited briefly and infrequently.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation of secret marriage plausible but inconsistencies in behavior and testimony reduce credibility.
propositions.quote: The claimant explained that the marriage was a secret, because the claimant's first wife had died of a serious illness two years previously, and both he and his new wife had adult children, and they feared the shame and embarrassment of their respective families. While the idea that for an older man in his sixties, now aged 70, marrying a wife with similar contextual issues, may present challenges to the existing families, is plausible, there are inconsistencies in the claimant's behavior and in the testimony and narrative that lead the panel not to trust the credibility of the claimant.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's secret marriage explanation is plausible but inconsistencies reduce credibility.

propositions.text: No marriage certificate presented; claimant's excuse insufficient given competent counsel and knowledge of procedures.
propositions.quote: There was no marriage certificate presented in the documents, and when asked about that, he said he didn't know he needed to present it and he could obtain it. The panel finds that this is an insufficient excuse considering the claimant was represented by extremely competent counsel, the claimant had been a Permanent Resident in the United States where he had lived for at least 6 years continuously so would have known the importance of documents for procedural matters, and applied for refugee protection since April 3, 2009.

propositions.text: Negative inference drawn from lack of documentation supporting secret marriage, an important claim element.
propositions.quote: The panel draws a negative inference from the lack of documentation to support the "secret marriage" considering it is an important element in his claim.

paragraphs.summary: No marriage certificate was presented; court draws negative inference from lack of documentation for secret marriage.

propositions.text: Claimant's explanation for fleeing to sister's house due to secret marriage unclear as some family knew and others did not.
propositions.quote: Later on the panel asked the claimant why he had chosen to flee to his eldest sister's in Bogota, rather than go to his wife's home? He replied that the marriage was a secret that no one in the family knew. As the hearing progressed it appeared that some family members knew, and other did not, so it was unclear how much of a secret it really was, and the reasons.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's explanation for fleeing to sister's house due to secret marriage is unclear as some family knew and others did not.

propositions.text: The panel asked the claimant about his living situation with his wife and family members in the house in XXXX.
propositions.quote: The panel asked the claimant about his allegation of having lived in the house belonging to his brother in XXXX, with his sister and brother-in-law, as the panel was trying to get a picture of what happened, and where the wife would have been

propositions.text: There is an inconsistency between the claimant's narrative and testimony about his wife's presence in the house.
propositions.quote: there is at this point an inherent inconsistency between the narrative and the testimony

propositions.text: The claimant said in the narrative he lived with his wife 2005-2009, but testified she lived there only from time to time.
propositions.quote: The claimant had stated in the narrative that he lived with his wife in this house during the period 2005-2009, and yet when questioned about her presence, he stated that she only lived there from time to time

propositions.text: At the time of the FARC event, only the claimant, his sister, her husband and a neighbor were present in the house.
propositions.quote: the only persons present at the time of the event in the house when the FARC arrived were himself, his sister, her husband and the neighbor

propositions.text: The panel was not fully concerned about the inconsistency because the wife might have had to attend to her own family.
propositions.quote: At this point the panel was not completely concerned, because it's possible that the wife had to turn her mind to her own family from time to time

paragraphs.summary: The panel found inconsistency between the claimant's narrative and testimony about his wife's presence but was not fully concerned, considering possible family reasons.

propositions.text: The claimant left XXXX to hide in Bogota but did not seek shelter at his wife's home, preferring his sister's.
propositions.quote: the claimant quickly left XXXX, to hide out in Bogota; however the claimant never sought shelter at his wife's home, in XXXX, preferring his sister's in Bogota

propositions.text: The claimant's choice to avoid his wife's home for fear of shame indicates lack of subjective fear of FARC.
propositions.quote: The fact that the claimant chose to go to his sisters' rather than his wife's for fear of shame, is an indication of lack of subjective fear

propositions.text: A reasonable person fearing FARC would seek help from a wife, even if the marriage was secret.
propositions.quote: a reasonable person would have sought help from a wife, whether a secret or not

propositions.text: The panel draws a negative inference from the claimant's behavior regarding fear and secrecy of marriage.
propositions.quote: the panel draws a negative inference from this behavior

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the claimant's choice to hide with his sister rather than his wife indicates lack of subjective fear and draws a negative inference.

propositions.text: The claimant said he left the village with his sister and her husband; his wife was living with her aunt in semi-hiding.
propositions.quote: The claimant replied that he was with his sister and her husband... he replied that she was living with her aunt, also in semi-hiding

propositions.text: The claimant said he did not live with his wife because her daughter was ill and the marriage was secret.
propositions.quote: Because her daughter is ill, and they don't know that we are married

propositions.text: From the wife's family side, it seems unreasonable that illness, fear, or secrecy would prevent hiding the claimant.
propositions.quote: it appears unreasonable that if the wife is in what was termed "semi-hiding" and if her daughter was seriously ill, that neither illness, fear of the FARC or the protection of a secret marriage would be a bar to hiding her husband

propositions.text: The panel draws a negative inference from the claimant's explanation about not living with his wife.
propositions.quote: The panel draws a negative inference from this

paragraphs.summary: The panel found the claimant's explanation for not living with his wife unreasonable and draws a negative inference from it.

propositions.text: The claimant and his first wife left Colombia in 1999 and obtained US permanent residence through their son.
propositions.quote: The claimant with his first wife, had left Colombia in 1999 and had obtained Permanent Residence status in the USA, as a result of the sponsorship of his son

propositions.text: A second son fled Colombia in 2001 due to FARC persecution and joined the family in the USA; a daughter came to Canada.
propositions.quote: A second son, fled Colombia due to FARC persecution in 2001 and joined the family in the USA. A daughter came to Canada

propositions.text: The claimant's first wife was diagnosed with terminal cancer, returned to Colombia, and died a month later.
propositions.quote: the claimant's first wife learned of having terminal cancer... she returned to Colombia... until she passed away, a month later

paragraphs.summary: The claimant and family left Colombia for the USA; his first wife died after returning to Colombia due to terminal cancer.

propositions.text: The claimant re-availed due to his wife's passing and then returned to the USA.
propositions.quote: The claimant re-availed due to her passing, and then returned to the USA

paragraphs.summary: The claimant re-availed after his wife's death and returned to the USA.

propositions.text: The claimant's son suffered severe mental depression, prompting the claimant to re-avail to Colombia in 2003 to remarry and enable his wife to return to the USA.
propositions.quote: The claimant's son... suffered a severe mental depression. The claimant re-availed to Colombia a second time in XXXX 2003, with the purpose of re-marrying, and enabling the wife to return to the USA

paragraphs.summary: The claimant re-avail to Colombia in 2003 to remarry and help his wife return to the USA due to his son's depression.

propositions.text: The claimant returned to Colombia in 2005, stayed at his brother's home, and abandoned his US permanent residence status.
propositions.quote: the claimant returned to Colombia, in 2005, and found a place to stay at the brother's home in XXXX, thus re-availing, and abandoning his US status

propositions.text: The claimant had US permanent residence since 1999 due to his son's sponsorship.
propositions.quote: The claimant had permanent residence in the United States since 1999, due to the son's ability to support

paragraphs.summary: The claimant returned to Colombia in 2005, stayed with his brother, and abandoned his US permanent residence.

propositions.text: Returning to Colombia briefly after wife's death is acceptable, but returning to marry in 2003 is different.
propositions.quote: While it can be viewed as acceptable to return for a brief time to re-avail due to the death of his wife, the panel finds that returning for the purpose of marriage is quite another matter, in 2003

propositions.text: The claimant alleges he married again in Colombia on XXXX, 2003.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleges that he had gotten married again in Colombia on XXXX, 2003

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds returning to marry in 2003 is different; the claimant alleges he remarried then.

propositions.text: The claimant re-availed a second time despite fear of FARC, prioritizing marriage over fear.
propositions.quote: this was a second time that he re-availed notwithstanding his fear of the FARC, as his desire to get married clearly overrode any fear he may have had

propositions.text: The claimant ignored potential fear despite his wife's brother and nephew being kidnapped in 2001.
propositions.quote: The claimant clearly chose to ignore any potential fear of FARC, because his wife's brother and nephew he alleged had been kidnapped as recently as XXXX in 2001

paragraphs.summary: The claimant re-availed despite fear of FARC, prioritizing marriage over fear, ignoring kidnappings in 2001.

propositions.text: The claimant said he and his children left Colombia due to FARC, but never claimed asylum in the USA as he was sponsored.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he and his children had left Colombia, because of the FARC, however the claimant had never claimed asylum in the USA; as he had been sponsored

paragraphs.summary: The claimant left Colombia due to FARC but never claimed asylum in the USA because he was sponsored.

propositions.text: The claimant lived in the USA with his first wife, who became ill and died; he described his life there as 'hell'.
propositions.quote: The claimant had lived in the USA, sponsored by his son, with his first wife, who had become ill and died. He said his life in the USA was "hell"

paragraphs.summary: The claimant lived in the USA with his first wife who died; he described his life there as 'hell'.

propositions.text: The claimant abandoned his US permanent residence status knowingly and did not maintain it.
propositions.quote: The claimant abandoned his permanent residence in the USA. He was asked if he knew that leaving for a certain period of time would lead to abandonment of status and he said, yes. He was asked if he took any steps to maintain his status and he said, no

propositions.text: The claimant did not maintain US status to assist his son, citing lack of capacity and son's family support.
propositions.quote: he responded that he did not have the capacity and the son had a wife and family

propositions.text: At the time he left the USA in 2005, he intended to stay in Colombia and abandoned US status due to marriage priority over fear.
propositions.quote: At the time he left the USA in 2005, he had turned his mind to staying in Colombia, and thus abandoned his status in the USA. The reason that he abandoned his status in the USA, was due to his marriage, which had taken priority over his fear

propositions.text: The panel concludes the claimant did not have a very strong fear of the FARC.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes then, that he did not have a very strong fear of the FARC

paragraphs.summary: The claimant knowingly abandoned US status due to marriage priority, showing weak fear of FARC, panel concludes.

propositions.text: The claimant's abandonment of US status indicates lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: As a result, the claimant's abandonment of status in the USA indicates a lack of subjective fear

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's abandonment of US status indicates lack of subjective fear.

propositions.text: The claimant's claim relies on an incident with inconsistencies in behavior and narrative versus testimony.
propositions.quote: The claimant relies on this particular incident, in XXXX for his claim, which contains inconsistencies in behavior and between the narrative and the testimony

propositions.text: The panel does not trust the claimant's credibility due to inconsistencies and behavior showing lack of subjective fear.
propositions.quote: the panel does not trust the credibility of the claimant. Furthermore the claimant's behavior shows a lack of subjective fear

propositions.text: The claimant re-availed a second time and abandoned US permanent residence, undermining his fear claim.
propositions.quote: due to the reason which lead him to re-avail a second time to Colombia, and in abandoning the safety of his permanent residence which he had enjoyed for 6 years

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds inconsistencies and behavior undermine claimant's credibility and subjective fear claim.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the claimant's claim.
propositions.quote: As a result the panel rejects the claim

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claimant's claim.

propositions.text: The claimant is not a Convention refugee.
propositions.quote: I find that the claimant is not a Convention refugee

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant is not a Convention refugee.

propositions.text: Due to lack of credibility, the claimant is not in need of protection from risk of life, cruel treatment, or torture if removed to Colombia.
propositions.quote: Due to the claimant's lack of credibility, and for the reasons above, I find that he is not a person in need of protection in that his removal to Colombia would not subject him personally to a risk to his life or to cruel or unusual treatment or punishment, or to a danger of torture

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant not in need of protection from risk of life or torture due to lack of credibility.

propositions.text: The claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: This claim is rejected

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects the claim.
